title: Birthday Bash
intro: [excited] Grab a party hat and a slice of cake, because tonight's episode is a BIRTHDAY BASH! Every category is wrapped up with a bow... [mischievously] and the only thing getting blown out tonight should be the candles, not your score.

art.prompt: Wide 16:9 festive title card: a whimsical birthday party table under a sunset sky, a towering three-tier pastel cake with sparkler candles, mismatched teacups and teapots, a bundle of colorful balloons drifting upward, streamers, confetti and wrapped presents, warm pink, gold and turquoise, painterly animation style. No people, no recognizable characters, no text or logos.

categories.title: A Very Merry Unbirthday
categories.intro: Our film category is 1951's Alice in Wonderland, home of the most famous unbirthday party ever thrown. [laughs] Statistically, today is probably YOUR unbirthday too, so congratulations!

art.prompt: 16:9 card art: a chaotic outdoor tea party in a surreal garden, a long table crowded with stacked teapots, teacups and an unbirthday cake with one candle, a giant pocket watch, oversized mushrooms and a crescent moon grin in the trees, bright storybook colors. No people, no recognizable characters, no text or logos.

clues.clue: The White Rabbit races through Wonderland worried that he is going to be this.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is late! [laughs] I'm late, I'm late, for a very important date. Honestly, that's me every morning before the show.

clues.clue: At the unbirthday tea party, the Mad Hatter is joined by this twitchy, tea-pouring hare.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is the March Hare! [chuckles] He and the Hatter would happily pour you a cup, then tell you to move down because there's no room. Rude.

clues.clue: Alice shrinks down to a tiny size after sipping from a bottle with this two word label.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Drink Me! [laughs] Later a cookie says Eat Me, and Alice shoots up like a beanstalk. Wonderland really needs a food safety inspector.

clues.clue: The Queen of Hearts plays croquet using these pink birds as mallets, with hedgehogs as the balls.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is... [chuckles] flamingos! The hedgehogs roll up as the balls. It's the least regulation croquet match in history, and the Queen still cheats.

clues.clue: This vaudeville comedian, famous for his wobbly giggle, voiced the Mad Hatter in the 1951 film.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Ed Wynn! [mischievously] The distractors were sneaky: Sterling Holloway was the Cheshire Cat, Jerry Colonna the March Hare, and Bill Thompson the White Rabbit.

categories.title: Party Animals
categories.intro: Party Animals is all about the birthday parties thrown inside Disney and Pixar films. [chuckles] RSVP required, presents optional.

art.prompt: 16:9 card art: a kid's bedroom birthday party with a cowboy-print wallpaper border, a pile of wrapped presents, party hats, floating paper lanterns glowing in the window, and a snowflake-decorated cake, joyful warm lighting. No people, no recognizable characters, no text or logos.

clues.clue: At Andy's birthday party in Toy Story, this space ranger arrives as a present and steals Woody's spot on the bed.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Buzz Lightyear! [excited] To infinity and beyond, and straight into Woody's jealousy zone.

clues.clue: Every year on Rapunzel's birthday, the kingdom of Corona releases thousands of these into the night sky.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is floating lanterns! [sighs] The king and queen launch them hoping their lost princess will come home. Have a tissue ready for that one.

clues.clue: In the 2015 short Frozen Fever, Elsa has a cold on Anna's birthday, and every sneeze creates these tiny snowmen.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is... [laughs] the snowgies! They end up living with Marshmallow up in the ice palace. Bless you, Elsa.

clues.clue: In Sleeping Beauty, the fairies fight over whether Aurora's birthday gown should be these two colors.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is pink and blue! [chuckles] Flora wants pink, Merryweather wants blue, and the dress keeps flipping right up to the final dance. I'm team blue, sorry Flora.

clues.clue: In Sleeping Beauty, this good fairy insists on baking Briar Rose's sixteenth birthday cake by hand, despite never having cooked before.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Fauna! [laughs] Her lopsided, candle-sliding cake is a true work of art. Eventually the wands come out and magic saves the day.

categories.title: Dressed for the Party
categories.intro: Everybody dresses up for a party! I'll show you a character's outfit broken down into colours... [mischievously] and you tell me who's wearing it.

art.prompt: 16:9 card art: a glamorous costume wardrobe for a party, rows of colorful outfits on hangers, fabric swatches and paint chips fanned out in rainbow order, a full-length mirror with a spotlight. No people, no recognizable characters, no text or logos.

clues.clue: These outfit colours belong to the birthday boy of November 18 himself.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Mickey Mouse! [laughs] Red shorts, yellow shoes, white gloves. Ninety plus years and he still hasn't changed his outfit.

clues.clue: This princess's dress colours are as famous as her apple.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is... Snow White! Blue bodice, yellow skirt, red bow. The fairest colour scheme of them all.

clues.clue: Howdy, partner! These colours belong to a pull-string toy sheriff.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Woody! [excited] Yellow plaid, a cow print vest, blue jeans and a red bandana. There's a snake in his boot, but not in this palette.

clues.clue: Orange shirt, black vest, blue pants, a floppy green hat. Gawrsh, who could it be?
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Goofy! [sarcastic] I gave you a hint with gawrsh, so if you missed it, I'm a little disappointed.

clues.clue: Yellow glow, a green dress, and bright blue hair. This colourful character lives inside a girl's head.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Joy from Inside Out! [chuckles] Sadness is blue all over and Disgust is green, so this one was a real brain teaser. Literally.

categories.title: Blow Out the Candles
categories.intro: Disney parks know how to throw a party, and they have birthdays of their own. [excited] Let's count some candles!

art.prompt: 16:9 card art: a fairy-tale castle silhouette at night lit by fireworks, a giant birthday cake shaped float in a parade street, golden ride vehicles shimmering, strings of lights over a Victorian main street. No people, no recognizable characters, no text or logos.

clues.clue: At Walt Disney World, guests celebrating a birthday can pick up one of these free at Guest Relations so cast members know to cheer.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is a birthday button! [excited] Wear it proudly and get ready for a whole lot of happy birthdays from complete strangers.

clues.clue: Disneyland in Anaheim opened its gates for the very first time on July 17 of this year.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is 1955! [laughs] Opening day was chaos: melting asphalt, broken drinking fountains, and way too many guests. Walt still called it a success.

clues.clue: This Walt Disney World park opened on Earth Day, April 22, 1998.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is... [chuckles] Animal Kingdom! A perfectly on brand birthday. The Tree of Life has been growing its party guest list ever since.

clues.clue: For Disneyland's 50th anniversary in 2005, one vehicle on each original 1955 ride, like a Dumbo and a teacup, was painted this colour.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is gold! [gasps] A golden Dumbo, a golden teacup, even a golden Jungle Cruise boat. I would have waited an extra hour just to ride the gold one.

clues.clue: EPCOT opened on October 1 of this year, exactly eleven years to the day after Magic Kingdom.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is... 1982! Magic Kingdom opened October 1, 1971, and EPCOT followed on October 1, 1982. Two parks, one shared birthday. Very efficient.

categories.title: Happy Birthday to Who?
categories.intro: Club DJ picked this one: famous Disney birthdays and ages. [whispers] If you know how old Ariel is, you're in GREAT shape.

art.prompt: 16:9 card art: a vintage calendar wall with circled dates, a row of cupcakes with candles of different ages, an old 1920s film reel and a steamboat whistle on a shelf, sepia mixed with bright party colors. No people, no recognizable characters, no text or logos.

clues.clue: Mickey Mouse's birthday is celebrated on November 18, the date this 1928 cartoon premiered in New York.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Steamboat Willie! [whispers] Plane Crazy was made first, but Steamboat Willie, with its synchronized sound, is the one that made Mickey a star.

clues.clue: Ariel tells King Triton she is not a child anymore, because she is this many years old.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is sixteen! [laughs] I'm sixteen years old, I'm not a child. Every dad watching just felt that one in their soul.

clues.clue: Tangled takes place as Rapunzel is about to celebrate this birthday.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is... [sighs] her eighteenth! Eighteen years of lanterns watched from a tower window, then one wild road trip with Flynn Rider.

clues.clue: Walt Disney was born in Chicago on December 5 of this year.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is... 1901! Walt was born in Chicago, grew up partly in Marceline, Missouri, and that small town Main Street shaped Disneyland forever.

clues.clue: Donald Duck's official birthday is June 9, the 1934 release date of this Silly Symphony, his screen debut.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is The Wise Little Hen! [laughs] Donald pretended to have a tummy ache to get out of work. Some things never change.
